architecture.mechanism: Carbon-based microwave susceptors with high surface area and porosity preferentially absorb microwave energy and convert it into localized heat, enabling targeted thermal processing at far lower bulk temperatures.
architecture.intervention: Line the microwave cavity floor or turntable with a thin carbon-based susceptor composite (e.g., graphite/activated carbon) sized to sit at the oven's field maxima, so it absorbs excess microwave energy at hot-spot locations and re-radiates it as diffuse thermal energy toward the food load, flattening the standing-wave pattern with no user action mid-cycle.
architecture.expected_effect: Hot spots at food edges are damped while the susceptor re-radiates energy toward cooler center regions, yielding a more uniform temperature distribution and reduced burning of edges.
architecture.falsification_test: Run identical cycles on a standardized load (e.g., agar gel block or bread slice) with and without the susceptor insert and compare thermal images; the mechanism is falsified if the with-susceptor trials show no statistically significant reduction in max-min temperature spread and edge-versus-center temperature variance across at least 10 paired runs.
